title: Model Spec (Textable, MLX (Apple Silicon), Mistral)
description: Model specification (scheme:identifier string identifying a machine-learning model).
documentation:
## Purpose
A model spec is a compact string that uniquely identifies a machine learning model
and tells the system where to find it. The format is `<scheme>:<identifier>` with
an optional query string for filtering (e.g. `hf:org/model-name?include=*Q8_0*`).
The scheme determines which backend or repository resolves the spec.

## Tag axes
The base anchor `model-spec` may be specialised along three orthogonal axes:
backend (gguf / mlx / candle), model-task (llm / vision / embeddings /
image-embeddings / transcription), and family (mistral / llama / phi / qwen).
Backend-agnostic specs simply omit the backend tag.

## Notes
The validation regex requires the scheme separator colon to be present and forbids
embedded whitespace in the identifier. Strings of up to 512 characters are allowed
to accommodate long query strings.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Backend
The inference framework or runtime that loads and executes a model. Backend choice
determines weight format, hardware acceleration, and runtime characteristics. A media
URN that omits the backend tag is backend-agnostic — it accepts any backend.

MLX is Apple's array framework for machine learning, native to Apple Silicon. Models
are stored as safetensors with MLX-specific config. Exploits the unified memory
architecture of M-series chips for fast, energy-efficient inference. Apple Silicon
only.

## Family
The model family — its architectural lineage. Families share chat templates, tokenizer
configurations, and structural assumptions. The runtime applies family-specific prompt
formatting (e.g. `[INST]/[/INST]` for Mistral, header_id for Llama 3) when invoking
inference. Family is detected from the model spec by content inspection.

Mistral and Mixtral family. Uses the `[INST]/[/INST]` chat template. Includes
Mistral-7B, Mistral-Nemo, Mixtral-8x7B and derivatives.
